claim: Lambda scaling changed on 2023-12-06 (What's New post date): each synchronously invoked function now scales by 1,000 concurrent executions every 10 seconds, independently of other functions, up to the account concurrency limit. Before, functions scaled at the account level by 500–3,000 concurrent executions (depending on the Region) in the first minute, then by 500 concurrent executions every minute.
question: How did Lambda's scaling rate change in 2023, and what did the older rule say?

values.spoken: a thousand every ten seconds, per function

values.display: followed by 500 concurrent executions every minute
values.spoken: the old rule: a burst, then five hundred per minute

qualifiers.scope: per function (new); per account and Region (old)
qualifiers.condition: up to the account concurrency limit

evidence.quote: Each synchronously invoked Lambda function now scales by 1,000 concurrent executions every 10 seconds until the aggregate concurrency across all functions reaches the account’s concurrency limit. In addition, each function within an account now scales independently from each other, no matter how the functions are invoked.

Before this update, Lambda functions could initially scale at the account level by 500–3,000 concurrent executions (depending on the Region) in the first minute, followed by 500 concurrent executions every minute until the account’s concurrency limit is reached.

changed.was: 500–3,000 concurrent executions (depending on the Region) in the first minute, followed by 500 concurrent executions every minute
